questions.question_text: What is the Geometrical shape of K4[Ni(CN)4]?
questions.answer: K4[Ni(CN)4] forms a tetrahedral complex due to the sp3 hybridization of Ni(II) when surrounded by four cyanide ligands.

questions.question_text: The crystal field theory considers the metal-ligand bond to be a _______ bond.
questions.answer: Crystal field theory assumes the metal-ligand bond as purely electrostatic (ionic) in nature, neglecting covalent interactions.

questions.question_text: The CFSE for a high spin d4 Octahedral complex is
questions.answer: For a high-spin d4 octahedral complex, the crystal field stabilization energy (CFSE) is calculated as -0.6Δoct.

questions.question_text: In a period with increase in atomic number, the metallic character of an element:
options: Increases across period and decrease in group
Increases across period and increase in group
Decreases across period and decrease in group
questions.answer: As you move across a period, effective nuclear charge increases, so nonmetallic character increases and metallic character decreases.

questions.question_text: HASB principle was given by
questions.answer: The Hard and Soft Acids and Bases (HSAB) principle was proposed by R.G. Pearson.
questions.chapter: Unit 1: Hard soft acids and bases

questions.question_text: Helmholtz free energy A is expressed
questions.answer: Helmholtz free energy is the energy available to do work at constant temperature and volume: A = U - TS.

questions.question_text: The anode of the galvanic cell has
questions.answer: In a galvanic cell, the anode is negative because oxidation releases electrons here.

questions.question_text: In corrosion, as a result of decay, the metals are NOT converted into
questions.answer: Corrosion typically leads to oxides, hydroxides, or carbonates of metals, but not peroxides.

questions.question_text: Chiral molecules which are non - super imposable mirror images of each other are called.
questions.answer: Enantiomers are chiral molecules that are non-superimposable mirror images of each other.

questions.question_text: The potential energy of n-butane is minimum for
questions.answer: Staggered conformation of n-butane has minimum repulsion, thus has minimum potential energy.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an initiator molecule in the free radical polymerisation?
questions.answer: Benzoyl peroxide is commonly used to generate free radicals for initiating polymerization reactions.

questions.question_text: A compound with the same molecular formula exists in two forms one is alcohol and the other is ether, what type of isomerism does it show?
questions.answer: Alcohols and ethers with the same formula but different functional groups show functional isomerism.

questions.question_text: The strength of the polymer increases with ______ in molecular weight
questions.answer: Higher molecular weight polymers have more chain entanglements, increasing their strength.
questions.chapter: Unit 4: Introduction to concept of macromolecules

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a natural polymer?
questions.answer: Rayon is a semi-synthetic polymer made from natural cellulose, not a true natural polymer.

questions.question_text: Intermolecular forces of thermoplastic polymers are
questions.answer: Thermoplastics have intermolecular forces intermediate between those of soft elastomers and strong fibers.

questions.question_text: Glass transition temperature (Tg) for Nylon - 6:6 is 50°C, which is higher than polyethylene due to
questions.answer: Nylon-6:6 shows higher Tg due to inter-molecular hydrogen bonding between polymer chains.

questions.question_text: Minimum interplanar spacing required for Bragg's diffraction is
questions.answer: Bragg's Law (nλ = 2d sinθ) shows the minimum interplanar spacing is λ/2 for first-order diffraction.

questions.question_text: The source for XPS is
questions.answer: Al K-alpha X-rays (AlKα, 1486.6 eV) are the commonly used excitation source for X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy (XPS).

questions.question_text: What happens in the case when the intermolecular distance increases due to tensile force?
options: there is no force between the molecules
there seems to be a repulsive force between the molecules
there seems to be an attractive force between the molecules
there is zero resultant force between the molecules
questions.answer: When molecules are pulled apart, the residual attractive forces dominate until separated far enough.

questions.question_text: Usually stronger constituent of a composite in
questions.answer: Reinforcement phase imparts strength and stiffness in a composite material, more than the matrix.
